referents.why: Third masculine singular 'him' of 'you will say to him' (cl5). The nearest agreeing referent in this verse is Pharaoh (w13), the one Moses is to stand before in cl2 and the addressee of the commanded speech.
referents.category: object pronoun of a commanded speech

referents.why: First person 'my' inside the LORD's quoted words (turn1, 'thus says the LORD: Let My people go'). A first person in someone's speech is that speaker, here the LORD (w25, sender of turn1), not Moses.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: First person 'me' in 'that they may serve me' (cl8) sits in the LORD's quoted words, so it is the speaker of turn1, the LORD (w25).
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: Imperative 'rise early in the morning' (cl1) in the LORD's speech to Moses (turn0). A command's implied 'you' is the person the command is spoken to, Moses (w4), the addressee of turn0.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to Moses

referents.why: Imperative 'present yourself before Pharaoh' (cl2) is in turn0 and addressed to Moses; the implied 'you' is Moses (w4).
referents.category: implied subject of a command to Moses

referents.why: Weqatal 'you will say to him' (cl5) is the LORD's command to Moses inside turn0; the implied 'you' is Moses (w4), the addressee of that speech.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to Moses

referents.why: Imperative 'let go my people' (cl7) is in turn1, the LORD's words delivered to Pharaoh. The implied 'you' is the addressee of the commanded speech, Pharaoh (w13), which agrees as second masculine singular.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: Yiqtol third masculine plural 'that they may serve me' (cl8) is the purpose of the release; its subject is 'my people' (w27). The noun is singular but collective, and Hebrew 'am takes a plural verb, so the morphology agrees.
referents.category: implied subject of a purpose clause

links.why: cl0 is the frame of the LORD's speech and opens the verse. cl3 ('behold') sits inside that speech, after the commands. A then-link continues the narrative line from an earlier clause, and cl0 has no earlier clause in this verse (across verses the episode rung applies, not this link).
links.category: then link from inside a speech back to its frame

links.why: Plain waw joining two commands to Moses, same person, no cause, result or purpose. Both clauses become command members of imp1.
cl5 is a weqatal ('and you will say to him'). A weqatal continues whatever it follows, so the saying follows Pharaoh going out (cl4). The waw is inside the verb, so and-then is the right relation.

The waw of cl8 joins a second-person command (cl7) to a yiqtol in a different person (third plural). The and type says a command joined to a change of person is so that, so the plain and is replaced by purpose.
links.category: command joined to a change of person

links.why: Command 'let go my people' followed by waw and a yiqtol in a different person, 'that they may serve me': what the release is for. It looks forward, as purpose does. The same clause is recorded as the aim of imp7.

groups.why: The LORD's speech to Moses. The builder listed cl1, cl2 and cl5 directly as parts. cl1 and cl2 are commands and move into imp1; cl5 is the frame of the commanded speech g1, which is nested here as a part. cl3 and cl4 stay as parts, the when-clause (see none_fit).
groups.category: commanded speech nested in a divine speech

groups.why: Two commands joined by a plain waw at one level form one imperative group with command members. The builder had cl2 as a part, which is the wrong role.
groups.category: commands joined by and at one level

groups.why: The commanded speech. The LORD tells Moses to say to Pharaoh what the LORD says, so the outer turn (turn0) has this turn as a part, and this turn has the LORD's words (turn1) as its part. Sender is Moses (the implied 'you' of cl5, w4); addressee is Pharaoh (the 'him' of cl5, w13).

The LORD's words delivered to Pharaoh. The builder listed cl7 and cl8 as direct parts. cl7 is the command and cl8 its aim, so the part is the imperative group imp7. The addressee is added as Pharaoh, which resolves the implied 'you' of cl7s.
groups.category: quoted divine speech with a command

groups.why: The yiqtol purpose clause cl8 qualifies the command to release the people, so it is the aim of the command, not a separate part of the speech.

none_fit.where: cl3 and cl4 ('behold, he is going out to the water'), giving the time at which cl2 is to happen
none_fit.what: A temporal clause, 'when Pharaoh goes out'. No link type says when for a clause like this. 'describing' needs a finite host right before it, and cl3 is an interjection; 'if' is a condition, not a time. They stay as parts of turn0 with no link.

cant_tell.what: Unlisted slot: the implied subject of cl4 (the participle 'going out', 'he')
cant_tell.why: The text fixes it as Pharaoh, the one Moses is to stand before, but the slot list does not carry this subject, so there is no slot id against which to record a choice. Flagged so the slot list can be checked.
